findings.message: Two different cases share one path. A work item that never opted in (no `fleet:auto` tag at all) is handled like a bad consent (tag added by someone else). Both call `refuse`, which sets the item to the mapped `Failed` state and tags it `fleet:refused`. The pipeline scans every approved change with `phase: proposal` on each run, so every approved change meant for a human gets moved to Failed in Boards. This contradicts the README, which says dispatch 'runs only when the work item carries the tag fleet:auto'. Fix: when `has_auto_tag` is false, skip without writing anything (for example, exit 3 or a new 'not opted in' code that the pipeline ignores). Keep `refuse` for a tag added by someone else, and for credential and vault failures.
findings.scenario: Approved change 050 is assigned to bob@contoso.com, who works it by hand, and its tags are 'specclaw'. Any later state.json commit on main triggers the pipeline. dispatch 050 → `consented` returns 1 → `refuse` → work item 050 System.State=Failed, tag fleet:refused, comment 'exit: refused: … has not consented'. Bob's in-progress item now shows Failed.

findings.message: AZDO_ORG is taken as `basename` of SYSTEM_COLLECTIONURI. That only works for `https://dev.azure.com/<org>/`. For the legacy `https://<org>.visualstudio.com/` form, which the README's egress list explicitly allows, the result is the whole host name. Every specclaw-azdo-issue call then goes to `dev.azure.com/<org>.visualstudio.com/...` and fails. Fix: parse both URL forms, or pass the org explicitly as a pipeline variable.
findings.scenario: SYSTEM_COLLECTIONURI=https://contoso.visualstudio.com/ → AZDO_ORG=contoso.visualstudio.com → `specclaw-azdo-issue show` requests https://dev.azure.com/contoso.visualstudio.com/... → 404 → dispatch dies with 'could not read the work item' → the step fails for every pending change.

findings.message: FLEET_REF is set from `$(Build.SourceBranchName)`. That variable holds only the last path segment of the branch, so it handles only single-segment branch names. A manual queue on any branch with a slash passes the wrong ref, while FLEET_COMMIT is that branch's HEAD. Fix: use `Build.SourceBranch` with the `refs/heads/` prefix removed.
findings.scenario: Pipeline queued manually on refs/heads/release/1.2 → FLEET_REF=1.2 → the pod's `git clone --branch 1.2` fails → work item marked Failed/clone-failed even though the dispatched commit exists on release/1.2.

findings.message: `attempt` counts the Jobs that currently carry the change label. That count is not the attempt number. The codex Job has a fixed name and `claim_codex_slot` deletes the previous finished one first. Claude Jobs are garbage-collected after `ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400`. Also, `label_value` collapses distinct change names (`049 x` and `049-x`) onto one label. So the recorded FleetAttempt resets or merges. Fix: derive the attempt from the work item's history or from a stored counter, not from live Jobs.
findings.scenario: Codex change 049-x: dispatch → succeeds → re-dispatch with --force. claim_codex_slot deletes fleet-codex-<h> and creates a new one → `get jobs -l specclaw.fleet/change=049-x` returns 1 → work item records attempt=1 for the second attempt. The same happens for a claude retry more than 24h later.

findings.message: The image that runs the agent decides the outcome, through the claude/codex versions and the specclaw plugin code baked into it. It defaults to the mutable tag `specclaw-fleet:latest`. The run record on the work item stores job, agent, cluster and commits, but not the image reference or its digest. Fix: record `image=$F_IMAGE`, and preferably the resolved digest, in `record_run`. Also require a digest or an explicit tag instead of defaulting to `:latest`.
findings.scenario: Two runs of the same change a day apart, with FLEET_IMAGE=specclaw-fleet:latest rebuilt in between: one reaches PR Open and one fails. Both work-item records are identical apart from the commits, so there is no way to tell which agent build produced each result.

findings.message: The tag split/trim/lowercase rule is still written several times: `has_auto_tag` (bash, consent.sh), `already_handled` (bash, workitem.sh), the jq `auto` def in `auto_tagged_by`, and PY_TAGS in specclaw-azdo-issue. They use different whitespace classes (bash `[[:space:]]`, Oniguruma `\s`, Python `str.strip`). Extract one bash tag-normaliser for the two bash copies.

The refusal message says '(add tag fleet:auto, or trigger the run yourself)'. Triggering the pipeline is no longer consent; both the README and the AC4d test say so. Drop 'or trigger the run yourself'.

BUILD_REQUESTEDFOREMAIL is still exported, and is still set in tests/cases/ac4_gates.sh, but nothing reads it since the requester-consent shortcut was removed. Remove it so it does not suggest that the requester affects consent.

The skill says dispatch 'refuses' an unapproved proposal or a missing work item, and lists exit 4 as 'refused'. The code `die`s with exit 1 for those two cases and does not tag them. Separate those two cases from the refusals in the doc.
The egress proxy image is the unpinned `ubuntu/squid:latest`. The README asks operators to pin it, but the shipped manifest does not. Pin it by digest.

`cmd_updates` removes its temp dir with `trap … RETURN`. Every `die` inside the paging loop exits the script without returning, so the dir is left behind on the failure paths. Use an EXIT trap, or clean up before each `die`.
